passage: I sat behind Tushar in the cafeteria when two boys from our own hostel block spilt trays and shouted at the staff. Tushar shrugged and said, "They just had a bad day." A week later two boys from the other block did the same thing, and Tushar said loudly, "Typical. Those people always behave like this." Ojas, at our table, raised an eyebrow. "You said bad day last week," said Ojas. Tushar blinked. "That was different." I could tell Tushar believed it. I do not think Tushar has noticed the double standard yet.

qa.q: What did Tushar say when two boys from Tushar's own hostel block spilt trays?
qa.a: Tushar said, "They just had a bad day."

qa.q: What does Tushar's "That was different" suggest about what Tushar believes?
qa.a: It suggests Tushar honestly believes the two cases differ and has not noticed the double standard; the blink shows surprise rather than deceit.

qa.q: What could Ojas do next time to help Tushar see it without an argument?
qa.a: Ojas could ask a gentle question, such as "What was different?", and let Tushar answer, instead of only pointing out the contradiction.

qa.q: How might Ojas be feeling when raising an eyebrow and repeating "You said bad day last week"?
qa.a: Ojas is probably a little puzzled or irritated by the unfairness, and speaks up while keeping the tone light enough to leave Tushar room to think.

grounding: A young adult sees a bad act by their own group as an individual mistake but a similar act by another group as typical, a double standard that feels natural.

passage: Monday. After the derby, three fans in Simran's club scarf threw bottles at the away stand. "A few idiots," Simran told Manjula. Wednesday. Photos showed three fans of the other club doing the same. "See? That whole club is savages," said Simran, scrolling. Manjula put down her phone. "Last week it was a few idiots." Saturday. Simran walked past the stand and saw both sets of fans clearing bottles together after a charity match. Simran remembered the words "a few idiots" and said to Manjula, "I said two different things about the same act." Manjula nodded.

qa.q: What did Simran say about the three fans in Simran's club scarf?
qa.a: Simran said they were "a few idiots".

qa.q: What was Simran feeling on Saturday when remembering "a few idiots"?
qa.a: Simran felt a jolt of realisation and some embarrassment at having judged the same act by two different standards.

qa.q: What turning point helped Simran notice the double standard?
qa.a: Manjula quietly repeated "Last week it was a few idiots", and later the sight of both sets of fans clearing bottles together made the contradiction plain.

qa.q: What might Manjula have been feeling when putting down her phone and repeating Simran's earlier words?
qa.a: Manjula was probably uneasy at the unfairness and chose a calm reminder rather than an accusation, leaving Simran room to notice.

grounding: A young adult sees a bad act by their own group as an individual mistake but a similar act by another group as typical, a double standard that goes unnoticed.
